title: Define root algorithm registry and fail-closed capability contract
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed new `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/algorithm.rs` and `capability.rs` (absent in V1); consumes ARCH-06 seam; no Fleet multicall work.
body:
## Outcome
Implement PKI-specific algorithm registry and typed capability report for Ed25519, P-256, RSA-4096, and standardized ML-DSA-44, covering key encoding, certificate/CRL signing and verification, CSR, CMS, and path verification independently. RSA-2048 is compatibility-only behind an explicit policy gate. No implementation is proposed for V1; this is V2 synthetic work.

## Current evidence
Intake census says V1 has no Fleet cert/pki domain. Public crate docs are evidence only for the named version/API surface, not Fleet integration. Use source-backed results in `research/pki-standards.md`; re-check pinned versions when implementing.

## Boundaries and acceptance
Own only PKI algorithm metadata and capability dispatch; consume ARCH-06's shared signer/artifact-authority seam rather than duplicating it. Produce a versioned per-operation matrix and synthetic smoke fixtures. A requested operation succeeds only when the exact adapter/version claims and proves it; independent verification is required for supported signatures. Oracle: adapter test result + independent verifier result, not parser success.

## Negative tests
Reject Dilithium2 as ML-DSA-44, unknown OID, absent primitive, unsupported key parameters, silent RSA-2048 substitution, unsupported ML-DSA client path, and provider-version mismatch.

## Safety and rollback
No production keys or provider writes. Any operator probe strictly parses all declared args before subprocess/network/write/lock; unknown args cause no side effects. Rollback disables the new registry entry/feature and preserves the diagnostic/test corpus; no serialized production state exists.

title: Implement PKI opaque identity, serial ledger, and manifest schema
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed new `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/model/identity.rs`, `manifest.rs`, `serial.rs`, and schema fixtures; shared opaque IDs owned by ARCH-01.
body:
## Outcome
Implement PKI object metadata for opaque stable IDs, issuer-scoped serial reservation, and versioned manifests. Identity is independent of subject/display name, filesystem path, DNS name, provider-native ID and logical secret path; paths remain mutable locators/attributes. Keep this PKI certificate/serial model scoped to CA artifacts and reference ARCH-01 for the shared opaque identity contract.

## Current evidence
V1 has no Fleet PKI. Spec §§5 and 7 describe IDs, serials and manifest; architecture review ADR-S01 requires stable opaque identity. Do not duplicate generic secret identity or storage work.

## Acceptance/oracle
Golden/property tests prove path/name changes do not change object ID, public/private manifest projections are deterministic and secret-free, and serial reservation is unique per issuer under concurrent synthetic requests. Manifest includes algorithm, key/cert IDs, parent, generation/partition/revision, DER/fingerprint, issuer, serial, SKI/AKI, validity, policy, provenance, public/private file index and validation receipts. Oracle: schema validation, stable canonical bytes, collision oracle and concurrency test.

## Negative tests
Reject ID derived from path/name, duplicate or nonpositive serial, out-of-range serial, path traversal, unknown schema/critical field, tampered hash, and private handle leakage. Do not assume portable CAS; guard levels are declared per adapter-operation and race tests do not treat lease/readback as serialization.

## Rollback
V2 fixtures only; migration rollback retains prior schema/ledger fixtures and uses a new schema version. Scripts validate whole argv before side effects. No provider or production write.

title: Generate four independent synthetic self-signed root identities
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§3.1, 5.1, 5.4, 10–11, 24.3; Appendix A PKI-001, PKI-017–020, PKI2-002
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed new `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/synthetic.rs` and X.509 fixture tests; no existing PKI crate or production storage.
body:
## Outcome
Generate an isolated synthetic set with exactly four independent root keys/certificates: Ed25519, P-256, RSA-4096 and ML-DSA-44. Reference notAfter is exactly `2050-07-07T12:00:00Z`; ordinary default remains 20 calendar years. Key-generation/storage ceremony approval (OPS-10 policy) is separate from certificate signature authorization. Each self-signature waits until final public SPKI, serial, exact dates and TBS hash are known, then uses ARCH-06's transaction-bound tuple. No V1 implementation, production key generation, or live root ceremony.

## Current evidence
V1 intake has no PKI. Spec §§3.1/24.3 and Appendix A PKI-001/PKI2-002 define the reference. Root custody and live execution remain unauthorized.

## Proposed files/API
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/synthetic.rs` creates synthetic key metadata and TBS; ARCH-06 signs only the final authorized tuple.

## Acceptance/oracle
Four distinct synthetic SPKIs/key identities and self-signed certs; exact signature/key algorithm OIDs and validity; subject default `C=US,O=developing.today LLC` and unique CA CN; CA extensions and SKI/AKI; manifest fingerprints and hashes match emitted bytes. Reject any authorization built before final SPKI/serial/TBS. Validate signatures and profiles using OpenSSL and independent capable Rust verifier; unsupported algorithm is reported unsupported.

## Negative tests
Reject reused key/SPKI, wrong algorithm/OID, RSA-2048 default, wrong timestamp, invalid CA constraints/usage, authorization hash mismatch or replay, bad self-signature and unknown extension.

## Rollback/safety
Only operation-owned synthetic fixture directory may be removed after ownership/hash check; never broad cleanup. Any script validates complete argv before writes/subprocess/network/lock. No live stores, signer authority, DNS or trust changes.

title: Construct and validate the nine-certificate asymmetric root graph
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed new `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/cross_cert.rs` and graph fixtures; no production signer or trust store.
body:
## Outcome
Create six directed cross-certificates among the three classical roots plus three classical-root-signed ML-DSA root certs, for nine cross-certs and 13 root certificate variants including four self-certs. ML-DSA root never signs a classical root by default. Cross-certs are path candidates, never trust anchors. Each cross-signature uses ARCH-06 authorization only after final subject SPKI, serial, dates and exact TBS are frozen.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI. The exact root graph is specified in §3.2; §24.2 reuses that root subset in the larger graph.

## Proposed files/API
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/cross_cert.rs` consumes ROOT-03 public key metadata and ARCH-06 signer capability. CERT-02 later composes this root subset into the complete root+issuer edge manifest; it is not a prerequisite for this root-specific acceptance.

## Acceptance/oracle
This issue's own manifest equals the exact nine-root-edge table in spec §3.2; every edge has correct subject SPKI, signer issuer/AKI, distinct serial/fingerprint, signature algorithm and exact `notAfter=2050-07-07T12:00:00Z` for every root variant. An earlier cap returns `ReferenceValidityMismatch` or requires an explicit non-reference profile and new authorization; it does not pass as reference. All 13 root variants are date-checked. Reject grants created before final tuple/TBS. Verify with OpenSSL and independent verifier for supported algorithms. Oracle is exact root-edge tuple equality plus cryptographic verification.

## Negative tests
Forbidden ML-DSA-to-classical edge, wrong signer/AKI/SPKI/date, expired/substituted edge, duplicate serial, cross-cert accepted as trust anchor, unauthorized/replayed tuple, or path that claims unsupported algorithm must fail.

## Rollback/safety
Revert/deactivate only synthetic graph version and retain evidence. Strict argument preflight before side effects; no production root signing or trust publication.

title: Bind root operation plans to shared transaction-bound signer authorization
stage: V2 PKI policy tests; V3 authorized root operations
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/authorization.rs`; generic signer/token contract and durable anti-replay belong to ARCH-06, this issue binds root-specific finite plans.
body:
## Outcome
Bind PKI root signature plans to ARCH-06's shared transaction-bound `SigningAuthorization`; do not implement a second generic signer/token interface. After public SPKI, serial, exact dates and TBS are frozen, enumerate finite exact tuples `(root signer fingerprint/handle + explicit source, subject SPKI identity, signature algorithm/parameters, profile/purpose, notBefore/notAfter, TBS SHA-256, authorized output/escrow destinations)` and canonical plan digest. Single tuple is default; bounded batch grants cover only that fixed set. Key-generation/storage ceremony approval is separate.

## Current evidence/status
V1 has no signer implementation; production signing is unauthorized. V2 tests use a fake ARCH-06 signer only. Shared authorization token/interface and durable consume implementation are ARCH-06; this issue owns root-specific tuple fields and integration.

## Proposed files/API
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/authorization.rs` prepares final root tuples and passes `SharedSigningAuthorizationRef` to ARCH-06; no generic Signer implementation.

## Acceptance/oracle
Race two consumers for one tuple: atomic durable consume permits at most one signer invocation. Inject crashes before consume, after consume/before signer call, after signer call/before receipt, after receipt, and lost response with no local receipt. An uncertain tuple stays burned until authoritative signer audit reconciliation; missing local receipt never implies unused. Oracle: durable tuple ledger, signer invocation count, and transaction+tuple receipt; no tuple may produce two signatures.

## Negative tests
Reject ambient/default discovery, signer substitution, grant before final SPKI/serial/dates/TBS, changed TBS/artifact digest, wrong subject/algorithm/purpose/dates/destination, expired/replayed grant, tuple addition after approval, blind retry of uncertain result, escrow read treated as authority, and key handle passed as ordinary secret ref.

## Rollback/safety
No real signer or key bytes in V2. Production root operations remain separate approval-gated work. On uncertain result preserve audit record and burn tuple until reconciled; never blind-retry. Operator scripts strictly validate argv before signer/store/network/file/lock side effects.

title: Build root-signer CRL ledger for root-issued CA certificates
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/crl_ledger.rs` and root-CRL fixture tests; CERT-09 owns issuer-signed leaf CRLs.
body:
## Outcome
Track root-issued CA certificates (root cross-certs and issuer CA cert variants) by actual root signer key ID + serial and build/verify synthetic root CRLs. This root-specific issuer-of-record ledger is separate from #9164 CERT-09, which owns issuer-signed leaf CRLs; #9164 CERT-10 owns stable CDP publication.

## Current evidence
V1 has no Fleet PKI or CRL service. Spec §§4.1/4.3/24.7 requires root CRLs cover intermediate and cross-certificates issued by that root, beginning with a real empty CRL and continuing with higher-numbered updates. No production signer/publication is authorized.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/crl_ledger.rs` consumes ARCH-06 signer capability; every CRL signature uses a finite per-signature plan tuple (root signer, CRL subject/issuer, signature scheme, purpose, thisUpdate/nextUpdate, exact TBS hash, destination scope). CERT-10 serves the unchanged original CDP URL for this root generation.

## Acceptance and independent oracle
Synthetic fixture enumerates signer-root → CA-cert edges and produces issuer-specific monotonic CRL number, thisUpdate/nextUpdate, AKI, revoked serial membership and immutable numbered artifact. Test sequence: publish empty root CRL, create a revoked root-issued cert fixture, publish higher CRL to configured mirrors, then fetch its original CDP and assert the newer CRL contains that serial. Oracle independently verifies signature, mirror hashes/freshness, actual signer-root serial ownership and fetched CRL content.

## Negative tests
Reject attribution to subject root instead of signing root, unknown cert edge, duplicate serial/CRL number, stale CRL, unauthorized or replayed CRL-sign tuple, incomplete initial empty CRL, CDP URL stuck at empty CRL, current route to another generation, lower CRL number and unsupported signature algorithm.

## Safety, dependencies and rollback
Synthetic only; no real revoke/sign/publish. Corrections use a new higher-numbered CRL and preserve history; never delete entries or roll CDP to a lower number. Operator wrappers strictly validate all argv before signer/file/network/lock effects.

title: Implement trust profiles and strict PQ-only path selection
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/trust.rs`, root-only trust bundle tests, and verifier integration; no global trust-store install.
body:
## Outcome
Generate roots-all, roots-classical and roots-pq bundles and deterministic candidate paths. Installable anchors are only selected self-signed roots; cross-certificates/intermediates stay untrusted. PQ-only requires ML-DSA root and ML-DSA signatures throughout; compatibility trust never claims PQ assurance.

## Current evidence
No Fleet trust feature exists in V1. Client algorithm support and trust stores are unverified per target/version.

## Acceptance/oracle
All-Ml-DSA synthetic path passes when verifier supports it; every classical leaf or any classical edge fails under PQ-only policy even if algorithm is supported. OpenSSL + independent Rust verifier results with pinned versions and actual chain bytes are the oracle; unsupported is not pass.

## Negative tests
Cross-cert as anchor, all-roots mislabeled PQ, classical fallback, unknown algorithm, invalid pathLen/AKI, unsupported signature and chain-order ambiguity reject.

## Rollback
Synthetic bundle/policy version can be deactivated; no auto-install. Trust installation is a separate privileged, approved operation. Strict arg parsing before installer/subprocess/privilege side effects.

title: Package public root artifacts and interoperable trust bundles
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§3.5, 7.1–7.2, 11.2, 24.9, 44; Appendix A PKI-028–035, PKI-059, PKI-069
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/bundle.rs` and root README/install templates; leaf handoff format remains CERT-12.
body:
## Outcome
Package public-only root bundles: manifest, PEM/DER, certs-only CMS when verified, trust subsets, cross-cert candidates, explicit chains, hashes and platform-specific install/verify/remove guidance. Do not duplicate leaf handoff format implementation; depend on #9164 CERT-12.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI artifact generation. Client installation capabilities vary; target/version claims must be evidenced.

## Acceptance/oracle
Public manifest/hash list matches exact bytes; PEM/DER consistency; CMS includes expected certs only; cross-certs are not trust anchors; OpenSSL and independent Rust validator agree on supported paths. Every guide is versioned or marked unverified.

## Negative tests
Reject private key in public archive, hash mismatch, wrong MIME/encoding, cross-cert in anchor bundle, unsupported client claimed supported, or SSH/X.509 confusion.

## Rollback/safety
Artifacts immutable by generation; rollback changes staged references, not bytes. No trust store changes or network publication. Strict argv validation before archive/filesystem/network action.

title: Build closed three-destination encrypted root escrow adapter
stage: V3 synthetic escrow adapter; live writes separately approval-blocked
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed optional `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/escrow.rs`; closed destination enum; ARCH-01/SEC-03 trusted scope policy and capability descriptors; no duplicate provider adapters.
body:
## Outcome
Implement the synthetic root escrow adapter for exactly encrypted laptop storage, authorized BWS project and authorized 1Password vault. Define independently encrypted per-root archives plus optional complete four-root bundle; no ordinary resolver, cache, prefetch, equality-index or generic replication. R2 remains research-only. Production writes remain a separate OPS-10 approval gate.

## Current evidence/status
Addendum requests these three destination classes but does not authorize production generation/export/write. Destination IDs, API/write modes, maximum encoded sizes, attachment behavior, and recovery identities are unverified; BWS values/notes are not general-purpose attachments. Synthetic adapter work is Backlog after ROOT-10 policy and SEC-03 capability descriptor; SEC-04/05 production adapters and real destination permissions are not needed for mock implementation.

## Broker and legacy-resolver rollout precondition
Before the first production copy, bind exact BWS project/native IDs and OP vault/item compartments in trusted policy. Ordinary broker and legacy resolver principals must be denied root-scope list/read where possible; otherwise a trusted pre-list exclusion must run before caching or name resolution. V1 broker refresh lists all accessible BWS records and caches values, while legacy name-only fallback can resolve accessible names. Caller-supplied DataClass or mutable sidecar is not authority; unknown/adopted records require classification review. Synthetic negative fixture: encrypted root archive appears in broker-compatible list and name-get paths; caller-visible list results omit its root identifier/name (or provider-side list is denied), it is excluded before cache, and legacy name-only get cannot return it.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/escrow.rs` consumes the closed policy and SEC-03 per-destination capability descriptor. Use fake destinations for synthetic tests; do not duplicate SEC-04/05 provider adapters.

## Acceptance/oracle
Preflight actual encrypted payload size and supported write format before writes; reject over-limit/unknown capability. If chunking is required, use immutable versioned chunks and an authenticated manifest with ordering, count, total encoded length, chunk lengths and hashes. Exercise synthetic readback/reconstruction, then restore each destination independently with the other two unavailable. Custody is complete only when all three independently restore; any partial/chunk/manifest mismatch is incomplete. Oracle: exact recovered fingerprints, archive integrity and synthetic sign/verify. No provider atomic commit/CAS is presumed.

## Negative tests
Reject extra destination/provider, R2, plaintext, unsupported attachment/format, wrong destination identity, truncation, over-limit, corrupt/reordered/missing chunks, wrong total length/hash, partial completion marker, stale archive, ordinary secret ref as root signer, generic cache/prefetch/equality-index enrollment, and recovery circularity.

## Rollback/safety
Only synthetic fixtures in adapter tests; no live key, vault write, export or provider operation. Production custody remains blocked under OPS-10 until separate explicit approval and destination verification. Stopping replication preserves verified versions; never auto-delete the last recoverable copy. Strict argv before provider/file/network/lock operations.

title: Specify root escrow payload, capability, and recovery policy
stage: V2 policy/design; restore is ROOT-09 acceptance
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/escrow_policy.rs` and recovery/chunk format schema; no provider writes.
body:
## Outcome
Before escrow adapter implementation, define per-root encrypted archives and optional complete bundle semantics, destination capability/size probes, format preflight, independent recovery recipients, and a chunk/manifest protocol if needed. Exact BWS/OP access/write limits are unverified. This issue is design-only; ROOT-09 implements synthetic adapter behavior and runs restoration acceptance afterward.

## Current evidence
Addendum §5 requests exactly encrypted laptop, authorized BWS project and authorized 1Password vault, but no production operation. BWS values/notes are not general-purpose attachments, and a complete four-root archive is not assumed to fit one object. No provider CAS or atomic commit is presumed.

## Trusted scope classification
Bind the closed root classification to provider scope/native IDs in trusted policy, not to caller assertions or mutable sidecars. Unknown/adopted records require classification review. Synthetic fixtures must show broker list/cache and legacy name-only lookup exclude registered root scopes before any live escrow copy is contemplated.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/escrow_policy.rs` defines closed destinations, archive variants, max-size checks and authenticated chunk-manifest schema. Provider capability descriptors/adapters remain SEC-03/04/05.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic capability fixtures demonstrate supported write formats and size boundaries; fail closed if capability or max size is unknown. Optional chunks have deterministic order/count/total length/per-chunk hash and authenticated manifest; reconstruction matches archive bytes. Specify the isolated restore procedure for each of three destinations with other two unavailable; no partial set is custody-complete. Oracle: policy schema, byte-for-byte reconstruction and ROOT-09 restore test.

## Negative tests
Reject assumption attachments/CAS/size are unlimited, silent truncation, missing/extra destination, R2 expansion, malformed chunk index/length/hash/order, shared recovery recipient stored inside its own archive, and recovery requiring the destination being restored.

## Rollback/safety
Design and synthetic fixtures only; no live key, vault, laptop secret or production archive. No network/store write. ROOT-09 depends on this policy; it is not a dependency of unrelated V2 PKI.

title: Design root lifecycle replacement and trust migration
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/root/lifecycle.rs` and migration runbook; actual leaf/issuer lifecycle remains CERT-08.
body:
## Outcome
Specify root renew-vs-rotate-vs-replace, new-generation trust overlap, dependent issuer inventory, client migration, deprecation and archival recovery over the long root lifetime. Keep active signing authority distinct from escrow and design future offline/HSM/external-signer migration without claiming hardware exists.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI; hardware/offline signer is future design, not current capability. Existing cross-domain issue dependencies should be referenced, not duplicated.

## Acceptance/oracle
State model and synthetic migration rehearsal prove new key identity/generation on rotate/replace; renew revision may preserve key only by explicit policy; old root remains available until dependents and clients verified; all paths retain receipts/CRL/public artifacts.

## Negative tests
Reject silent key reuse, removal of trust before overlap, destruction of historical CRLs, unsupported recovery, and a design that assumes root public cert alone recovers private key.

## Rollback
Stop activation and return to prior trust package while valid; never reverse a signed event by deleting the root. Production ceremony separately approved.

title: Define production root ceremony and explicit approval gates
stage: V4 production ceremony only after owner authorization
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed operator ceremony docs and PKI preflight under `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/`; never execute production actions from this issue absent separate authorization.
body:
## Outcome
Produce a reviewed ceremony runbook/preflight for any eventual production root generation, signature, escrow, publication or trust action. It must bind transaction authorization to key fingerprint, subject SPKI/algorithm, purpose, exact validity, artifact-plan digest, authorized destinations, expiry, transaction ID and single-use default; enumerate exact three escrow destinations and independent restore checks.

## Current evidence/status
This design does not authorize production operations. Keep Blocked until the owner supplies explicit applicable approval, custody identities, reviewed rollback and independent witness.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic dry-run emits exact artifacts/actions/approvals and proves no live side effect. Before the first escrow copy, verified native-scope registration and ordinary broker/legacy resolver exclusion are hard rollout preconditions. Missing/expired/wrong-scope approval or unverified isolation prevents signer invocation, store/network write, DNS or trust mutation; no new BWS project is created by this design. Preflight-to-apply evidence can demonstrate external edits are not overwritten under unguarded conflict-sensitive target; oracle is protected external value plus `needs_review`/conflict receipt.

## Negative tests
Ambient signer lookup, replayed grant, changed artifact digest, unauthorized destination, incomplete three-copy restore, broad `--yes`, unexplained unguarded write and partial mirror must stop.

## Rollback/safety
No live run under this issue unless separately authorized. Before signing, abort/no-op; after signing preserve key/certificate and evidence, halt publication and follow incident plan. Never claim key deletion reverses issuance. Strict complete argv parse before any side effect.

Design the PKI facade types for purpose, issuer set/key/cert identity, CSR/leaf request, signer authorization, receipt and injected clock/entropy/sink. This issue owns PKI-specific contracts only; shared CLI registry, secret identities and general provider framework remain in #9157/#9158.

title: Freeze the explicit 65-certificate signer graph
source_ranges: sources/fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§3.2–3.3, 24.2, 30, 33.2, 48.2 V3-S15; Appendix A PKI-001–008, PKI2-004–008, PKI-068

body:
## Outcome
Publish the exact §24.2 edge manifest for 4 root keys/13 root cert variants and 16 issuer keys/52 issuer cert variants, 65 total CA certs before leaves. The source gives 13 issuer certs per purpose/partition; two purposes × two partitions = 52. One-per-issuer-key baseline is 16 with 36 additional signer variants, explanatory arithmetic only. There is no unresolved user split or pending approval.

## Current evidence
V1 intake has no Fleet PKI. Spec §24.2 and architecture-review.md ADR-S04 are the controlling explicit matrix. `pki_graph.py` is a pure synthetic edge/count/date oracle, not crypto evidence.

## Proposed files/API
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/tests/reference_graph.rs` compares generated manifests with `reference-graph-v1.json`; root certificate construction is ROOT-03/04, issuer construction is CERT-06.

## Acceptance/oracle
Machine-readable row per cert: opaque subject key ID, signer root ID, signature algorithm, purpose/partition, cert role, expiry and eligibility. Assert exact 20 keys/65 CA certs, 4 self+9 root-cross variants, 52 issuer variants, 13 per purpose/partition, all 13 roots exact `2050-07-07T12:00:00Z` and all 52 issuers exact `2032-07-07T12:00:00Z` in reference mode; earlier caps fail reference mode or require explicit non-reference profile/new authorization. Compare complete tuple set against §24.2.

## Negative tests
Reject any missing/extra edge, duplicate identity, A/B key alias, ML-DSA-root-to-classical, wrong count/date, or count-only test without exact edge-set equality.

## Rollback
Graph schema revisions are versioned; signed/published graph is never rewritten. Supersede by new version and preserve prior evidence. V2 uses synthetic data only; no production signing.

title: Implement algorithm/object-specific PKI signer adapters
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§10, 24.3, 33.3; Appendix A PKI-008, PKI2-008, PKI-071/074

body:
## Outcome
Implement PKI-specific algorithm/object capability reporting and adapters through ARCH-06's shared signer/authorization interface. Do not duplicate the generic signer trait, token format, or durable replay journal. Signing authorization is minted only after final public SPKI, reserved serial, exact dates/extensions and TBS/artifact hash exist; key-generation/storage ceremony approval is separate.

## Current evidence
No V1 PKI signer or provider implementation. `research/pki-standards.md` gives documentation-level boundaries, not Fleet capability or a validated dependency. No production signer is authorized.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/signer_adapter.rs`, per-operation `PkiSignerCapabilities`, and synthetic adapter tests; ARCH-06 owns generic signer contract, durable authorization consumption, receipt and anti-replay.

## Acceptance/oracle
For each algorithm/object pair, versioned capability entry matches an isolated fixture proof. Adapter passes exact TBS and finite authorized tuple to ARCH-06 and independently verifies receipt/signature. Reject any grant built before final SPKI, serial, dates and TBS exist. Race two consumers for one tuple: at most one atomic durable consume and signer invocation. Inject crashes before consume, after consume/before call, after call/before receipt, and after receipt; lost/uncertain result remains burned until authoritative signer audit reconciliation. Oracle: durable tuple ledger/invocation count + independently verified signature. Unsupported operation returns typed error before signer invocation.

## Negative tests
Reject silent ML-DSA/Dilithium substitution, algorithm/backend/signature mismatch, wrong explicit source, altered tuple/TBS, pre-final grant, tuple addition after approval, expired/replayed/consumed tuple, concurrent second consumer, unsupported object, provider-version mismatch or fallback signer.

## Rollback
Disable optional adapter/feature and preserve receipt/test corpus. No production key material, provider writes, or ordinary-cache access.

title: Build strict CSR parser and proof-of-possession validator
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§10, 24; Appendix A PKI-014, PKI-026, PKI-045; RFC 2986
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/csr.rs` and parser corpus; no general import adapter.
body:
## Outcome
Add bounded PKCS#10 DER/PEM CSR inspection and PoP verification. CSR subject, SPKI, SAN and extension requests are untrusted proposals; issuer policy creates final extensions. This is PKI parser work only, not general artifact import.

## Current evidence
No Fleet PKI in V1; RFC 2986 defines CSR shape and PoP, not CA issuance policy.

## Acceptance/oracle
Known-good synthetic CSR accepted; parsed SPKI matches eventual cert; OpenSSL independently inspects/validates fixture. Parse bounds and typed errors; no signer invocation during invalid preflight.

## Negative tests
Malformed/oversized DER, invalid PoP, unknown critical extension/OID, duplicate extension, unsupported parameters, path traversal filename, requested SAN outside policy and SPKI mismatch reject before signer.

## Rollback
No raw CSR persistence by default; remove only operation-owned test file. Strict CLI arguments before file/network/signer side effects.

title: Define purpose profiles, extension policy, and SAN/wildcard validator
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§3.3–3.4, 24.6, 44; Appendix A PKI-015–016, PKI-023–027; RFC 5280; RFC 9525
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/profile.rs` and `san.rs`; client policy fixtures separate from issuing engine.
body:
## Outcome
Implement Base/InternalWeb typed profiles, certificate KU/EKU/pathLen/name constraints, SAN normalization, and wildcard validation. Web apex+wildcard shorthand yields four exact names for the two reference domains. Public trust is not implied by public DNS.

## Current evidence
No V1 PKI. RFC 9525 requires full leftmost wildcard semantics; client enforcement of name constraints varies and must be tested.

## Acceptance/oracle
Canonical SAN list/property tests, pinned public-suffix test data, independent hostname verifier; Web uses serverAuth and SAN; no CN fallback. Oracle: expected normalized identities and target verifier result.

## Negative tests
Reject multi-label/multiple wildcard, embedded `*`, wildcard IP/URI/email, public suffix, malformed IDNA, constrained-out SAN, CN-only hostname, excessive KU/EKU and algorithm-incompatible usage.

## Rollback
Profiles are immutable/versioned; correct via new version. Synthetic only. Strict argument validation before signer or output side effects.

title: Implement issuer-set synthetic builder and graph verification
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§24.2–24.5, 33.2; Appendix A PKI-009–PKI-022, PKI2-002–009, PKI-068
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/issuer.rs` and issuer graph fixtures; ROOT owns root graph/custody, CERT-06 owns issuer A/B outputs.
body:
## Outcome
Generate synthetic Base and Internal Web issuer A/B keys and the exact frozen §24.2 graph; produce manifest and deterministic artifacts. ROOT owns root graph/custody; this issue owns issuer keys/cert variants. Key-generation/storage ceremony approval is separate from each signature authorization.

## Current evidence
No Fleet PKI in V1. Spec §24.2 directly gives 13 certs per purpose/partition and 52 total issuer certs. CERT-02 serializes that literal matrix; no invented split or approval is pending.

## Proposed files/API
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/issuer.rs`. Flow: generate/test key → verify SPKI → durably reserve serial → freeze TBS and date/extensions → request ARCH-06 grant bound to final tuple → atomic consume → sign/verify.

## Acceptance/oracle
16 distinct issuer keys; exactly 52 variants under CERT-02; all 52 issuer certs use exact `2032-07-07T12:00:00Z` in reference mode; an earlier parent/profile cap fails reference mode or requires explicit non-reference profile/new authorization. Exact CA extensions, subject, SKI/AKI, unique issuer serial, and signatures independently validated. Grant binds final SPKI, serial, dates, purpose, signer and TBS hash. Oracle: exact edge-set plus manifest/date assertions and independent cryptographic verification.

## Negative tests
Forbidden ML-DSA-root/classical issuer, duplicate A/B or purpose key, validity beyond root, wrong KU/pathLen, profile drift, duplicate serial, missing CRL prerequisite, grant minted before final SPKI/serial/TBS, tuple mismatch or replay.

## Rollback
Synthetic fixtures only; retain serial gaps and failure receipts. No production signer/store/publication. Strict complete argv parse before keygen/sign/write/lock/network.

title: Implement leaf issuance API/CLI and fast in-memory mode
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§6, 9, 24.6, 48; Appendix A PKI-023–027, PKI-051–052, PKI-055–057
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/leaf.rs` and thin registry entry in Fleet CLI only after ARCH-07; API/CLI share request model.
body:
## Outcome
Issue synthetic Base test leaf and InternalWeb leaf through the same typed library and Fleet CLI contract. Fast mode returns in-memory artifacts without documentation or network work. Multiple selected algorithms produce separate keys/certs, never one multialgorithm cert.

## Current evidence
No V1 Fleet PKI. CLI names/examples in source are proposed, not executable commands.

## Acceptance/oracle
Base 1y test identity and Web SAN leaf; exact SPKI and chain; validity bounded by parent; API/CLI output oracle agrees. Private key remains in test handle by default. Verify with OpenSSL plus independent Rust verifier where supported.

## Negative tests
Web no SAN, CSR unauthorized SAN, invalid wildcard, expired parent, leaf expiry beyond issuer, unavailable algorithm, key/signature mismatch, private key in public-only output, and PQ policy fallback reject.

## Rollback
Stage only synthetic artifacts; retain previous fixture until new is verified. Strict whole-argv parse before signer/output/network/lock side effects.

title: Add renew/rotate/replace state and safe resume
stage: V2 synthetic lifecycle, V3 guarded activation
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/lifecycle.rs` and model tests; no root ceremony implementation.
body:
## Outcome
Implement distinct cert renew/reissue, key rotate, and orchestrated replace states with resumable receipts. Renew preserves key only under explicit policy and increments cert revision/serial; rotate creates independent key and generation.

## Current evidence
No V1 implementation. Spec §5.2 distinguishes lifecycle terms and requires trust overlap.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic state-model tests prove identity/revision transitions, idempotent resume, no double signing, and new generation trust plan; exact manifest IDs are oracle. Inject interruption at every stage.

## Negative tests
Reject silent key reuse on rotate, claim of rotation without new SPKI, expiry beyond parent, retry with changed request hash, removal of old trust before verified overlap.

## Rollback
Before activation cancel; after signing preserve artifacts/serial evidence; after publication do not delete immutable objects; use explicit alias/trust overlap recovery. No production operation without approval.

title: Build CRL state, signing, and lifecycle ledger
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§4.3, 10–11, 24.7, 44.1; Appendix A PKI-033, PKI-036; RFC 5280
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/issuer_crl.rs`; root-signed cert CRL ledger is ROOT-06.
body:
## Outcome
Implement synthetic per-signing-CA revocation ledger and signed CRL build/verify. ROOT-06 owns root CRLs for issuer/cross-certificates actually signed by a root; this issue owns issuer-signed leaf CRLs. Create signed empty CRL before a CDP-bearing certificate becomes publishable, then support later monotonic CRL updates.

## Current evidence
No live CRLs or endpoint. Spec §§4.1/4.3/24.7 requires initial empty CRL plus subsequent updates. OCSP is separately deferred.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/issuer_crl.rs`; signer calls consume finite CRL signature tuples via ARCH-06, publication/CDP URLs are CERT-10.

## Acceptance/oracle
Monotonic issuer-specific CRL number, signed thisUpdate/nextUpdate, correct issuer/AKI, only authorized serial membership; independently verify signature. Test sequence: create empty CRL and cert embedding CDP; revoke synthetic leaf; build/publish next CRL; GET the certificate's original unchanged CDP URL and assert it serves a higher-number CRL containing that serial. Oracle: parsed signed CRL and original-URL fetched bytes, not an alias plan.

## Negative tests
Wrong signer/CRL owner, stale CRL, duplicate serial/CRL number, missing empty CRL, unauthorized revoke, phantom `good`, root cross-cert on subject rather than signer CRL, lower CRL number at original CDP, wrong generation, or missing mirror rejects.

## Rollback
Revocation is append-only; correct with next CRL, never remove historical CRL/entry or roll current CDP to a lower number. Production revoke/sign/publish remains approval-gated; strict argv before signer/network/write/lock.

title: Construct durable CDP and immutable CRL publication plans
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/publication/plan.rs` and local HTTP fixture tests; no deployment adapter enabled.
body:
## Outcome
Build immutable numbered CRL archive objects plus a durable stable current-CDP URL per signing-key/generation; AIA certificate variants stay immutable. Leaf AIA names issuer candidates; CDP names the actual signer's current CRL; cross-signed CA AIA/CDP point to the signing root. The certificate's original CDP URL must continue serving successive verified monotonic CRLs for that same authority.

## Current evidence
`pki.developing.today` is illustrative, not verified deployed. AIA retrieval is opportunistic, and client revocation refresh/enforcement varies. No network publication is authorized.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/publication/plan.rs`, per-key/generation CDP route contract, and local HTTP fixture; production publisher/DNS remains separately gated.

## Acceptance/oracle
Local HTTP sequence: publish signed empty CRL; issue synthetic cert with original CDP URL; revoke test serial; publish higher-numbered CRL to all three configured mirrors; verify bytes/signature/issuer/freshness on each; only then advance stable CDP route. GET the certificate's original CDP URL and assert higher CRL contains serial. `Cache-Control max-age` is bounded by `nextUpdate`; ETag/Expires/revalidation behavior is tested. Oracle is fetched bytes parsed as a valid signed CRL, not URI config alone.

## Negative tests
Bare directory URI, mutable AIA variant, wrong issuer/generation, missing initial CRL, stale mirror, lower current CRL number, unbounded cache lifetime, false OCSP URI, bad MIME, HTTPS bootstrap redirect, auth barrier, mismatch hash, path traversal or promotion before mirror verification reject.

## Rollback
Numbered CRL archives remain immutable. Never move current CDP to a lower CRL number; recover through a corrected higher-numbered CRL. Staged local fixtures only; no DNS/network production change. Strict arguments before network/file/lock effects.

title: Add staged publication and guard-aware alias receipts
stage: V2 local/mock publisher; V3 separately approved deploy
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/publication/adapter.rs` and fault tests; generic artifact authority seam is ARCH-06.
body:
## Outcome
Implement publication state/receipts for immutable objects and controlled current-CDP routes. Declare guard level per adapter+operation as `atomic-precondition | serialized-by-contract | unguarded`; BWS/op/bw are unguarded until primary documentation plus isolated test proves otherwise. Conflict-sensitive promotion requires a guarded level or stops `needs_review`; only separately approved named weaker policy can proceed and must state lost-update window in plan+receipt. Additive immutable CRL archive writes are not gated by that conflict rule.

## Current evidence
V1 has no Fleet PKI publisher or verified `pki.*` hosting. AIA/CDP hostnames are illustrative. ADR-S02/A-1 says no portable CAS; Fleet lease/readback does not serialize external writers, and BWS/op/bw are unguarded absent primary documentation plus isolated proof.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/publication/adapter.rs` implements only the PKI adapter to ARCH-06 artifact authority; no generic publisher or queue writer.

## Acceptance/oracle
For a conflicting mutable pointer, default preflight → external edit → apply preserves external value and reports conflict/unsupported-guard. If an approved weaker mode is tested, assert disclosed risk and do not claim concurrent value preservation. CRL-specific oracle: publish initial empty CRL, then revoke, publish+verify higher CRL on all configured mirrors, and fetch original CDP URL to confirm revoked serial; never promote pointer before all mirrors are fresh/valid.

## Negative tests
Reject assumed CAS, Fleet lease as serialization, silent overwrite, weaker policy without named approval/window, current CDP pointer moving to lower CRL number or different signer/generation, stale/mismatched mirror, unbounded cache policy, and retry without idempotency key.

## Rollback/safety
No production publish in V2. Numbered archives stay immutable; current CDP only advances. Rollback of other aliases requires proven guard; report cache residuals. Strict argv parse before network/write/lock/deploy.

title: Implement certificates-only CMS and delivery kit formats
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§4.2, 7.1–7.5, 24.9; Appendix A PKI-028–035, PKI-048, PKI-055; RFC 5652
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/formats/{cms,chain,kit}.rs` and cert-only CMS fixtures; no private key export.
body:
## Outcome
Produce PEM/DER, certs-only CMS/P7C and precomposed chain artifacts for minimal/public-only/handoff kits. Private formats require a separately authorized encrypted destination; SSH/PGP/JWT stay native and separate.

## Current evidence
No Fleet kit implementation in V1. RFC 5652 defines CMS structure; Rust crate docs do not alone prove full workflow.

## Acceptance/oracle
CMS parser verifies degenerate SignedData/no signers and expected certificate fingerprints; DER/PEM roundtrip exact certs; chain order and MIME match manifest. Independent parser/verifier tests and corpus are oracle.

## Negative tests
Reject signed CMS mistaken as certs-only, unexpected cert/private key, wrong MIME, chain rooted in untrusted cross-cert as anchor, unsupported format/algorithm, `.crt` extension assumed to mean DER, SSH certificate represented as X.509.

## Rollback
Artifacts are versioned and immutable; revert kit pointer, never overwrite. No private export or production distribution; strict args before archive/file operations.

title: Implement trust-profile export, install plan, and test matrix
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§3.5, 11.1–11.2, 44, 48.2; Appendix A PKI-006–007, PKI-035, PKI-059, PKI-061–062
stage: V2 synthetic export/test; V3 install approval
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/trust_export.rs` and tested consumer matrix; root graph owned by ROOT-07.
body:
## Outcome
Export roots-all/classical/PQ bundles and explicit install plans by OS/client. Cross-certs and intermediates are untrusted path candidates. This owns #9164 trust handoff; root graph belongs to #9163.

## Current evidence
V1 has no trust installer. Client and algorithm support unverified; docs must name versions and mark unsupported accurately.

## Acceptance/oracle
Independent OpenSSL and Rust path verification with explicit chains; PQ-only accepts all-ML-DSA path and rejects any classical leaf/signature; all-roots never labeled PQ. Install plan is non-mutating; where testable target client confirms fingerprints.

## Negative tests
Cross-cert imported as anchor, unsupported client success claim, automatic global trust modification, malformed chain, classical fallback in PQ profile, and SSH/X.509 conflation.

## Rollback
Export-only is safe. Install is separate privileged approved action with exact fingerprint and scope; removal plan touches only installed fingerprints and maintains overlap.

title: Keep OCSP explicitly unsupported unless responder is complete
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§4.3, 24.7, 33.2, 48.2 V3-S22; Appendix A PKI-033, PKI2-022; RFC 6960; note.md unsupported class
stage: V1 design decision; V2 negative capability test
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/ocsp_capability.rs` and absence tests only; no responder implementation.
body:
## Outcome
Keep OCSP URI absent and capability explicitly unsupported unless a real responder has issuer routing, status DB, authorization, key custody, freshness, rate limits, request validation, audit and independent tests for each issuer/algorithm. OpenBao ML-DSA limitation remains unsupported, not an alternate success path.

## Current evidence
No OCSP endpoint exists in V1. RFC 6960 `good` does not prove issuance. Research note records crate ASN.1 support as distinct from operational responder support.

## Acceptance/oracle
Capability output says unsupported; no OCSP AIA extension when service is absent. Fake query for unknown issuer/algorithm never returns synthetic `good`; implement RFC state distinctions and tests only if future responder separately approved.

## Negative tests
Phantom URL, `good` from absence in stale CRL, responder key unauthorized, issuer routing confusion, unsupported ML-DSA response, wrong freshness and no status DB all fail closed.

## Rollback
Keep feature disabled; removing unused capability has no production effect. Any future responder is a new reviewed issue, never part of this ticket's scope.

title: Generate DNS and publication runbooks without applying them
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed generated `PUBLISH.md`, `publish-plan.yaml`, `dns.zone`, and schema fixtures under PKI bundle templates; no live DNS writes.
body:
## Outcome
Generate validated BIND zone fragment plus provider-neutral DNS/publication change manifest and PUBLISH/README instructions with relative source paths, exact target URLs, MIME, hashes, cache/revocation notes, validation and rollback. Generation never applies DNS.

## Current evidence
No domain record or PKI distribution host verified; `pki.*` names are proposed placeholders. CAA authorizes public CA issuance, not private CA. CT is generally public WebPKI; private CA has its own ledger.

## Acceptance/oracle
Zone parser and schema validate; every plan path maps to a generated artifact; unresolved placeholders cannot execute. Docs distinguish ACME/DCV/CAA/CT and private trust. Oracle is parser + file/URL/hash consistency.

## Negative tests
Invalid zone syntax, placeholder treated as live, fabricated DNS diff, private CA described as browser-public, CAA treated as private CA authorization, and DNS mutation in generation tests reject.

## Rollback
Docs/plan files are versioned; no DNS operation exists. Strict args before file/network actions.

title: Add issuance state, journaling, and failure recovery
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§6, 10, 24–25, 48; Appendix A PKI-043, PKI-047, PKI-049–050, PKI-054–057
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/operation.rs` and model/failure-injection tests; shared journal/outbox belongs to OPS-01/OPS-03.
body:
## Outcome
Implement append-only PKI operation states, request hashes, actor/approval, signer receipt, artifact hash, idempotency and resumable batch state on #9157's shared journal/receipt contract. Do not duplicate the general Fleet journal/outbox.

## Current evidence
V1 PKI is absent. Architecture ADR-S02 classifies per-adapter/per-operation writes; BWS/op/bw are unguarded until primary evidence plus isolated test proves otherwise. A Fleet lease/readback is not serialization.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/operation.rs` records PKI state and references shared #9157 journal types; per-operation guard status and plan/receipt fields support CERT-11.

## Acceptance/oracle
Inject failure before signer, after signer, CRL build, staging, upload, alias, and activation. Default unguarded conflict test does not apply and reports `needs_review`; preflight → external edit → apply leaves external value recoverable and reports conflict. A separately approved named weaker-policy test must show the lost-update window in plan+receipt and does not claim preservation. Ensure no serial reuse, duplicate signer invocation, false active status, or blind retry. Oracle is generated state schedule plus receipt and store readback.

## Negative tests
Reject last-success advancement without readback, lease-as-serialization, blind replay after uncertain timeout, partial CRL mirror, mutable-CDP rollback to lower number, overwrite after concurrent edit, and omitted weaker-policy disclosure. Additive immutable creates/history remain allowed.

## Rollback
Preserve signed/published evidence; resume only with exact request hash/authorization receipt; never delete immutable artifacts; strict whole argv before all side effects.

title: Prove backend compatibility and independent validation per artifact
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§9, 11.2, 35, 48; Appendix A PKI-061–064, PKI-070, PKI-074; research/pki-standards.md

## Outcome
Maintain version-pinned capability evidence for rcgen, x509-cert/RustCrypto, OpenSSL and independent path verifiers by algorithm and object type: cert, CSR, CRL, CMS, external signer. Recheck before dependency adoption.

## Current evidence
`research/pki-standards.md` has retrieved RFC and docs.rs capability boundaries; it is not proof that any crate supports the complete Fleet graph or is integrated.

## Acceptance/oracle
Per-operation table cites primary docs/source, versions, enabled features/platform, executable safe fixture and independent verifier output. Unsupported capability clearly marked unsupported. Oracle is executable output plus independently validated signature/profile.

## Negative tests
Do not infer signing from ASN.1 parser; path validation from DER parsing; HSM support from trait shape; ML-DSA from Dilithium; or complete issuance from library name. Reject silent substitution.

## Rollback
No prod dependencies or key operations. Version bump invalidates evidence and reruns corpus; remove optional adapter feature while preserving interface.

title: Stage guarded production issuance and publication approvals
owned_files_or_interfaces: Proposed `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/approval.rs` and operator preflight contract; provider custody implementation remains SEC/ROOT owners; shared signer seam is ARCH-06.
body:
## Outcome
Design approval policy for scoped issuance, publication and trust operations. Bind every root signature to transaction `SigningAuthorization`; restrict root escrow to closed three-destination policy. Model adapter-operation guard level and halt conflict-sensitive unguarded apply unless separately approved named weaker policy carries lost-update window in plan+receipt.

## Current evidence/status
No live root signer, vault permission, DNS target or trust install is authorized. This issue remains Blocked. Synthetic dry-run may validate policy but cannot self-authorize production.

## Acceptance/oracle
Preflight displays exact objects, signer, authorization, destinations and effects. Missing/expired/wrong-scope approval produces zero signer/provider/network calls. Conflict injection preserves external edit and reports conflict. Publication only starts after independent verify and CRL readiness.

## Negative tests
Ambient signing, replayed authorization, unknown escrow destination, incomplete restore, unguarded overwrite, `--force` bypass, stale/missing CRL, and auto trust/DNS mutation all block.

## Rollback
Before signing no-op; after signature preserve artifacts/audit, do not claim reversal; post-publication immutable objects remain and alias rollback is guard-capability dependent. Never operate without separately documented owner authorization.

title: Prepare offline and hardware signer migration rehearsal
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§24.3, 33.3, 40, 48; ADDENDUM_secrets_architecture_performance_infrastructure.md §5; Appendix A PKI-044, PKI-071, PKI-074
owned_files_or_interfaces: Research/runbook only; future `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/signer_migration.rs` if a later approved implementation is scheduled.
body:
## Outcome
Research and rehearse an adapter migration from temporary approved custody to offline/HSM/PKCS#11/KMS/external signer, preserving explicit transaction-bound authorization, historic roots, recovery and trust overlap. No hardware capability is claimed now.

## Current evidence
V1 has no Fleet PKI or verified HSM. Addendum asks for future offline/hardware path; architecture review ADR-S05 requires independent restoration.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic migration verifies public key identity/fingerprint, exact TBS signature and receipt across adapter change; outage/restore, new/old trust overlap and independent archive recovery rehearsed. Source-backed capability matrix distinguishes hardware-tested from API-theoretical support.

## Negative tests
Reject implicit signer fallback, key export without approval, root handle used as ordinary secret, unsupported attestation claim, changed subject key, removal of old root before dependent-client proof.

## Rollback
Return only to a still-authorized prior signer and preserve trust overlap; no production migration without separate approval. Research is nonblocking for V2 synthetic graph.
